stories.headline: MISSILES FALL AS POLISH JETS SCRAMBLE
stories.summary: RUSSIA SENT ABOUT 400 DRONES AND 110 MISSILES AT UKRAINE OVERNIGHT, KILLING AT LEAST EIGHT PEOPLE AND STRIKING POWER AND HEATING SITES AS WINTER SETS IN. SOME MISSILES CROSSED BRIEFLY INTO POLISH AIRSPACE, AND POLISH AND ALLIED AIRCRAFT WERE SCRAMBLED IN RESPONSE. WARSAW CALLED IT A SERIOUS PROVOCATION BUT HELD BACK FROM CALLING IT A DIRECT ATTACK.

stories.headline: TRUMP MEETS XI AND PUTIN AS SUMMIT OPENS
stories.summary: THE PRESIDENT MET THE CHINESE AND RUSSIAN LEADERS ON THE SIDELINES OF THE ASIA SUMMIT. HE SAID US FIRMS THAT BUILD DATA CENTRES ABROAD WOULD FACE RESTRICTIONS UNLESS THEY KEPT AMERICAN JOBS AT HOME, A THREAT AIMED SQUARELY AT THE CHIP AND COMPUTE INDUSTRY.

stories.headline: KYIV SECURITY GUARANTEE TIED TO CEASEFIRE
stories.summary: NEGOTIATORS FLOATED A NATO-STYLE SECURITY GUARANTEE FOR UKRAINE, WITH SIGNATORIES COMMITTED TO AID IF THE COUNTRY IS ATTACKED AGAIN. THE ARRANGEMENT WOULD BIND A CEASEFIRE THAT MOSCOW HAS SO FAR REFUSED TO ACCEPT, AND OFFICIALS SAID THE TEXT REMAINS OPEN.

stories.headline: SENATE REJECTS WAR-POWERS CHALLENGE
stories.summary: THE SENATE VOTED DOWN A RESOLUTION THAT WOULD HAVE FORCED A HALT TO MILITARY ACTION AGAINST IRAN WITHOUT CONGRESSIONAL APPROVAL. THE MEASURE FAILED AS A SLIM BIPARTISAN GROUP BROKE WITH PARTY LINES, LEAVING THE ADMINISTRATION'S HAND FREE FOR NOW.

stories.headline: WAGE PROTESTS SWEEP ACROSS EUROPE
stories.summary: WORKERS IN MORE THAN 25 EUROPEAN COUNTRIES MARCHED FOR HIGHER PAY, ARGUING THAT WAGES HAVE LAGGED BEHIND FOOD, RENT AND ENERGY COSTS FOR A THIRD YEAR. ORGANISERS DEMANDED INDEXED PAY SCALES AND NATIONAL MINIMUM WAGE RISES.

wire: POLAND SAID MISSILE DEBRIS FELL NEAR A BORDER VILLAGE, WITH NO INJURIES REPORTED.
THE SUMMIT CLOSED WITH A COMMUNIQUE ON SUPPLY CHAINS AND SEA LANES.
THE SENATE VOTE ON THE WAR-POWERS RESOLUTION WAS 47 FOR AND 52 AGAINST.
